statement: ▶ Conjecture 11. For each ∆ and q ≥ 2∆ there is an FPRAS for counting the number of q-list packings of graphs of maximum degree ∆.
context: vertex. The history of this problem suggests that further generalizations, e.g. to list packing may not be straightforward. While one can consider analogous dynamics for list packings and hope to reduce the bound on q in Theorem 1, we do not have results showing the existence of list packings in graphs of maximum degree ∆ for fewer than 2∆ − 2 colors. In another direction, the use of more advanced Markov chain techniques to give perfect sampling of list packings could be interesting. We finish with a natural conjecture on approximately counting list packings. ▶ Conjecture 11. For each ∆ and q ≥ 2∆ there is an FPRAS for counting the number of q-list packings of graphs of maximum degree ∆. At the time of writing, we know of no reason that the lower bound on q cannot be reduced to, say, ∆ + 1. The value 2∆ represents a significant barrier in the sense that the existence of a list packing when q ≥ 2∆ is an elementary consequence of Hall’s theorem (though arguably not entirely trivial).
